note: Track caged (guitar-caged), step 2: the A shape: open A moved up as a barre, the chord, arpeggio, pentatonic and scale in the same frets, in three keys, then C in the A shape and the E shape.

exercise.title: CAGED: the A shape
exercise.why: A barre chord with its root on the A string is the open A chord moved up the neck, so a chord you know in the E shape has a second place, with its own arpeggio, pentatonic and scale around it.

cells.text:
Press the chord box below to hear A. Then press the three chord boxes under it: each is the same shape moved up the neck, with finger 1 in place of the nut.
Play all four, and say each chord's name as you land on it: the name is the note under finger 1 on the A string.

Press Play on each of the four panels below to hear it: the chord, its arpeggio, the pentatonic and the scale, all in the same frets.
Play each one on your guitar, starting and ending on a root, until you can see the chord inside the scale.
Then try another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key.
When you change the key, the shape moves along the neck and every note keeps its place inside it.

Press Play below to hear the arpeggio run up and back down. Then play it yourself, from the lowest {{1}} to the highest note and back.
Keep going until your fingers find the next note without you looking.

Press Play on the two chord panels below to hear C in the A shape, then higher up in the E shape. Play one, then the other, on your guitar.
When you change the shape, the chord keeps its name and its notes, and only their places on the neck are new.
